notes: The book was copied in Cāvela village (Chabahil, also spelled Cāvahil), near Paśupati and Guhyeśvarī. 'cavivela gaṇeśā sase' probably means 'beside the Cāvahil Gaṇeśa' (Chabahil Gaṇeśa temple). 'Hilavāla' is probably a family or clan name and is kept as a title. 'Amvaradhoja' is the Nepali form of Ambaradhvaja. The era is unspecified ('samvat … sāla'), but the Nepali phrasing ('sāla mīti', 'roja') points to Vikrama Saṃvat, which gives 1881 CE for VS 1938. The weekday was not checked against the tithi. The catalogue fields agree with this reading.
